Platelet-rich plasma versus hyaluronic acid injection for knee osteoarthritis: a randomized controlled trial

Statistical analysis

Statistical analysis was performed using IBM SPSS Statistics, version 28.0 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA). Shapiro-Wilk test and histograms were used to evaluate the normality of the distribution of data. Quantitative parametric data were presented as mean and standard deviation (SD) and were analyzed by unpaired Student's t-test (or Welch's t-test when Levene's test indicated unequal variances). Quantitative non-parametric data were presented as median and interquartile range (IQR) and were analyzed by Mann-Whitney test. Qualitative variables were presented as frequency and percentage (%) and were analyzed utilizing the Chi-square test or Fisher's exact test when appropriate. Effect estimates were reported as mean differences, Hodges-Lehmann median differences and relative risks (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) was used to compare groups after adjustment for covariates, reporting adjusted (estimated marginal) means with 95% CI and Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons. A two tailed P value ≤ 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

Results

In this study, 83 patients were assessed for eligibility; 20 patients were excluded (not meeting inclusion criteria: 14; declined to participate: 6). The remaining 63 patients were randomly allocated into two groups (PRP group: 32, HA group: 31). In PRP group, 2 patients were lost to follow-up (Moved away (n=1), withdrew consent (n=1)). In HA group, 1 patient was lost to follow-up (Withdrew consent). Finally, 30 patients in PRP group, 30 patients in HA group were analyzed statistically.

Discussion points

WOMAC at (M1, M3 and M6) was significantly lower in PRP group than HA group. The size of this difference over time should be judged against its minimal clinically important difference. VAS at (M1, M3 and M6) was significantly lower in PRP group than HA group. The size of this difference over time should be judged against its minimal clinically important difference.

Conclusion

In conclusion, WOMAC at (M1, M3 and M6) was significantly lower in PRP group than HA group.
